1.concept: 反意疑问句 — Question tag — she'd / would
1.zh: “这是好消息。她一定会很高兴，不是吗？”我问茜蒂。
1.note: 附加问句 (Question tag)：陈述含 would 肯定式，用 wouldn't + 主语；与 she'd 情态一致。

2.zh: 亚当为我们打开大门之前，我们无法离开大院。
2.note: 时间连词：not … until 表示“直到……才”；before 表在此之前，与否定主句搭配不当。

3.concept: 感官动词 — Perception verb — spot + -ing
3.zh: 贝蒂看见爸爸在洗车时，赶紧朝他走去。
3.note: 感官动词 spot 后接宾语 + 现在分词，表示看见正在进行的动作。

4.zh: 双胞胎躺在床上翻来覆去，直到午夜过后才睡着。
4.note: 一般过去时：lie（躺）的过去式是 lay；laid 为及物“放置”的过去式。

5.zh: 若我父母有机会旅行，他们会带上我。
5.note: 第二类条件句 (Second conditional)：与现在事实相反或不太可能，主句用 would + 动词原形。

6.zh: 尽管罗德尼只会一点韩语，他仍喜欢在韩国度假。
6.note: 数量词：little + 不可数名词；few + 可数复数。

7.zh: 若功课需要帮助，请去找老师。
7.note: 情态动词 should 表建议；shall 多用于第一人称疑问，must 过强。

8.zh: 因为害羞，我几乎不与邻居和同学交流。
8.note: 副词 hardly 表“几乎不”，含否定意义；与 shy 语境一致。

9.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject–verb agreement — number of
9.zh: 知道名额有限，我哥哥上周就预订了。
9.note: 主谓一致：the number of + 复数名词仍用单数谓语；过去叙述用 was。

10.zh: 学校应学生要求组织了多场工作坊。
10.note: 固定搭配 in response to 表示“回应、针对”。

11.stem_plain: They were once best friends but _________ when they could not agree on the title of the project.

12.stem_plain: Mrs Lee was _________ making sacrifices for her son but he was unaware of her efforts.

13.stem_plain: As we explored the abandoned mansion, a strange creaking sound caused me to _________ .

11.zh: 他们曾是挚友，却因项目标题意见不合而闹翻了。
11.note: 选（3）fell out：好友因分歧不再和好。fell in/off/through 义为陷入、跌落、计划落空，不符。
11.concept: 词汇辨析 — fell out（闹翻；脱落）

choices.eg: He fell in love with music at an early age.
Sales fell off after the holiday season.
They fell out over a silly misunderstanding.
Our picnic plans fell through because of rain.

12.zh: 李太太不断为儿子牺牲，儿子却不知道她的付出。
12.note: 选（4）constantly：强调持续不断地牺牲。其余偏“严格/顺利”，不合频率义。

choices.eg: Rules are strictly enforced in the laboratory.
The event ran smoothly from start to finish.
Data was rigorously checked before publication.
She constantly reminded him to be polite.

13.zh: 探索废弃宅邸时，奇怪的吱呀声把我吓了一大跳。
13.note: 选（4）jump out of my skin：突然惊吓。break a leg / get out of hand / turn a blind eye 为其他习语。
13.concept: 词汇辨析 — jump out of my skin（吓一大跳）

choices.eg: Actors say break a leg before a show.
The party got out of hand after midnight.
He turned a blind eye to the litter.
The bang made me jump out of my skin.

14.zh: 吴太太听说赢得五万元现金奖，震惊得晕头转向。
14.note: 选（1）reeling：极度震惊、头昏目眩。fainting 指昏倒；faltering/hopping 不合语境。
14.concept: 词汇辨析 — reeling（晕眩；震惊不已）

choices.eg: She was reeling from the unexpected news.
He came close to fainting in the heat.
His voice was faltering with nerves.
Children were hopping across the playground.

15.zh: 宜尽快提交表格，逾期不予受理。
15.note: 选（2）advisable：建议尽快交表。compulsory 过强；tolerable/permissible 语义不符。
15.concept: 词汇辨析 — advisable（明智的；宜于）

choices.eg: The noise was barely tolerable.
It is advisable to arrive early.
Small bags are permissible in the hall.
Attendance is compulsory for all pupils.

cloze: Ta Li was a tall and strong boy who was fond of fighting. Those who were younger and smaller felt [Q16 (intimidated)]. Ta Li often said that he was [Q17 (second to none)]. He would without any reason, bully people [Q18 (at will)]. "Yesterday, he ordered me to do all his homework. How [Q19 (tyrannical)]!" Kumar complained.
"Once, I saw him standing outside the principal's room. When I asked what happened to him, he told me to mind my own business!" Joshua grumbled.

[Q20 (Out of the blue)], Ta Li appeared from behind them. "You two! Carry my bags!" he commanded. Kumar and Joshua ignored him. Ta Li then rushed forward and tried to punch them. But, the boys told him that they would report him to their teacher if he did. Knowing the consequences, Ta Li turned around and stormed off.
zh: 塔力是个高大强壮、爱打架的男孩。年纪小、个子矮的同学都感到害怕。塔力常说自己天下无敌，还无缘无故欺负人，想怎样就怎样。“昨天他逼我把作业全做了，多霸道！”库马尔抱怨道。
“有一次我看见他站在校长室外。我问怎么了，他叫我别多管闲事！”约书亚嘟囔道。
塔力突然从两人身后冒出来。“你们两个！替我拿包！”他命令道。库马尔和约书亚不理他。塔力冲上前要揍他们，男孩们说再这样就要报告老师。知道后果后，塔力转身气呼呼走了。

16.concept: 近义词 — intimidated（极度害怕的）
16.zh: 年纪小、个子矮的同学都感到极度害怕。
16.note: 应选（2）'terrified'：intimidated 指被威吓、害怕。worried 程度较轻；helpless/ashamed 不合霸凌语境。

choices.eg: Parents were worried about the storm.
The smaller boys felt terrified of Ta Li.
They felt helpless against the flood.
He felt ashamed of his rude remark.

17.concept: 近义词 — second to none（最好的）
17.zh: 塔力常说自己天下无敌（最好）。
17.note: 应选（2）'the best'：second to none = 无人能及、最好。the first/tallest/winner 误解习语。

choices.eg: She was the first to finish.
His skills are the best in the team.
He is the tallest in class.
She was declared the winner.

18.concept: 近义词 — at will（随心所欲地）
18.zh: 他无缘无故、想怎样欺负就怎样欺负人。
18.note: 应选（1）'as he so wished'：at will = 任意、随心。其余为 as long/much/frequently，义不同。

choices.eg: He bullied others as he so wished.
Stay as long as he could.
Eat as much as he could.
Train as frequently as possible.

19.concept: 近义词 — tyrannical（不公而残暴的）
19.zh: “他逼我做全部作业，多霸道残暴！”库马尔抱怨。
19.note: 应选（4）'unjustly cruel'：tyrannical 指专横残暴。indolent/arrogant/unintelligent 不合“霸道”义。

choices.eg: An indolent student rarely finishes homework.
His arrogant tone offended everyone.
The plan was unintelligent and costly.
The ruler was unjustly cruel to villagers.

20.concept: 近义词 — Out of the blue（出乎意料地）
20.zh: 塔力出乎意料地从他们身后出现。
20.note: 应选（4）'Unexpectedly'：out of the blue = 突然、没想到。Abruptly 偏突兀；Sneakily/Immediately 不合习语。

choices.eg: The meeting ended Abruptly.
He Sneakily took an extra cookie.
Reply Immediately if you can.
Ta Li appeared Unexpectedly from behind them.

21.stem_plain: What is the objective of this flyer?

options.2: To teach participants the art of positive thinking.
options.3: To encourage people to sign up for this workshop.
options.4: To provide participants with a life-changing experience.

22.stem_plain: What is the purpose of the questions on page 6?

options.1: To make the writer's thinking visible to readers.
options.2: To check whether the readers have understood the flyer.
options.3: To give readers some ideas what the workshop is about.
options.4: To arouse the readers' interest in finding out more about the workshop.

options.1: mainly students who give up easily
options.2: people who are inspired by Eddie Chan's famous quote
options.3: only parents whose children are addicted to their mobile devices
options.4: anyone who wishes to learn how to lead a happy and healthy lifestyle

24.stem_plain: Which one of the following will **not** be shared at the workshop?

options.4: Ways to create a positive future for yourself

25.stem_plain: What does **'this'** under the sub-heading "What do the experts say?" refer to?

options.2: the ability to recover from setbacks
options.3: putting in more effort to achieve the goals

26.stem_plain: **'Let's Hear From Our Participants'** is a suitable sub-heading because _________.

options.1: participants get to express their opinions about the workshop
options.2: the organiser wants participants to feel satisfied with the workshop
options.3: readers know that parents and their children can attend the workshop
options.4: the organiser is glad to learn that Jason Li and David Li liked the workshop

27.stem_plain: According to the flyer, we know that Mr Eddie Chan _________.

options.1: has been a trainer for more than 30 years
options.2: will be conducting this workshop for the last time
options.3: will be inviting his participants to share their success stories
options.4: is a firm believer of positive thinking after he became a trainer

28.stem_plain: Which one of the following statements about the flyer is **not** true?

options.1: There will be a hands-on activity.
options.2: Participants stand a chance to win prizes.
options.3: Registration for the workshop will close on 1 November 2021.
options.4: Participants can go online to find out more about the workshop.

21.concept: 主旨 — Main purpose — sign-up（主要目的）
21.note: Flyer promotes a workshop with registration details → main aim is to encourage people to sign up, not merely publicise the organiser or promise a vague “life-changing” experience without the call to register.

22.concept: 题型 — Rhetorical questions — interest（题型考点）
22.note: Questions on page 6 invite readers to reflect and arouse interest in finding out more, rather than testing comprehension or only listing workshop topics.

23.concept: 题型 — Target audience（题型考点）
23.note: Workshop welcomes anyone who wishes to learn how to lead a happy and healthy lifestyle — not limited to quitters, quote fans, or parents of phone-addicted children only.

24.concept: 题型 — NOT shared — avoid pessimists（题型考点）
24.note: Flyer covers healthy eating, stress, positive future; it does not promise teaching how to avoid pessimistic people as a workshop topic.

25.note: Under “What do the experts say?”, this refers to being energised, independent and optimistic — qualities linked to resilience after setbacks, not merely setting higher goals or effort alone.

26.concept: 题型 — Sub-heading function（题型考点）
26.note: ‘Let’s Hear From Our Participants’ shows participants get to express their opinions about the workshop through testimonials.

27.concept: 题型 — Trainer detail — last time（题型考点）
27.note: Flyer states Eddie Chan will be conducting this workshop for the last time — a time-limited offer, not 30 years as trainer or inviting success stories from participants.

28.concept: 判断 — NOT true — closing date（找出错误项）
28.note: Registration does not close on 1 November 2021 according to the flyer — option (3) is false. Hands-on activity, prizes, and online info are supported.

cloze: Hagfishes are soft-skinned creatures without scales. [Q29] known as slime eels, these unique living things can be found in the depths of the ocean. Depending on the species, they can grow [Q30] to one metre long. Having [Q31] a tail fin but no jaws or bones makes hagfishes very unusual marine animals. [Q32] other creatures, their mouths are either round [Q33] thin. Hagfishes cannot see very well. [Q34] their other senses are very sharp. Compared to other fishes, they have far more gills — about five to fifteen pairs of gills [Q35] are used for breathing under water.

Hagfishes, preferring to lie buried in the sand, [Q36] be found in cold seawater. Their diet comprises mainly dead and sometimes crippled fishes. Sometimes, [Q37] the disadvantage of fishermen, hagfishes attack the fishes that the fishermen have caught. They then eat their way [Q38] the bodies of the fishes and consume the fishes from the inside out. Their feeding habits are disgusting but help to clean up dead fish on the ocean floor.
zh: 盲鳗是没有鳞片的软皮生物，也被称为黏液鳗，这种独特的生物生活在深海。不同种类可长到一米左右。只有尾鳍却没有颌骨和骨骼，使盲鳗成为非常奇特的海洋动物。与其他生物不同，它们的嘴要么圆要么扁。盲鳗视力很差，然而其他感官非常敏锐。与其他鱼类相比，它们鳃更多——大约五到十五对鳃，用于水下呼吸。
盲鳗喜欢埋在沙里，可在寒冷海水中找到。它们主要以死鱼为食，有时也吃受伤的鱼。有时对渔民不利，盲鳗会攻击渔民已捕获的鱼，从鱼体内吃进去，把鱼从里到外吃掉。它们的进食习惯令人作呕，却有助于清理海底死鱼。

29.note: also known as slime eels, these = 结合句意选 also。

30.concept: 短语动词 — grow up to
30.note: the species, they can grow up to one metre long. = 结合句意选 up。

31.note: Having only a tail fin but no = 结合句意选 only。

32.note: unlike other creatures, their mouths are = 结合句意选 unlike。

34.note: however their other senses are very = 结合句意选 however。

35.note: to fifteen pairs of gills which are used for breathing under = 定语/名词性从句 → which。

36.note: lie buried in the sand, can be found in cold seawater. = 情态动词 can。

37.note: Sometimes, to the disadvantage of fishermen, hagfishes = 看前后搭配，选 to。

38.note: They then eat their way into the bodies of the fishes = 看前后搭配，选 into。

cloze: It is now mandatory for diners to return their trays and clear their table litter. Table litter [Q39(include)] used tissues, wet wipes, straws, canned drinks, plastic bottles and food [Q40(remmnents)] . As part of an effort to help diners adjust to this practice, no disciplinary action will be [Q41(take)] until after 31 August 2021. Until then, diners will only be advised to [Q42(following)] the rule. However, from 1 September 2021, [Q43(enforsemant)] of this law will apply to those who are caught not [Q44(complied)] with advice to clean up after themselves. First-time [Q45(ofendars)] will be given a written warning. The Singapore Food Agency will also [Q46(works)] with the National Environment Agency (NEA) to roll out the [Q47(implement)] in the fourth quarter of this year [Q48(progresively)] . NEA said the move, which comes amid a public health [Q49(crissis)] , followed years of extensive [Q50(educasional)] efforts. These have been undertaken to change behaviour and mindsets of diners in public places.
zh: 现在食客必须归还托盘并清理桌上垃圾。垃圾包括用过的纸巾、湿巾、吸管、罐装饮料、塑料瓶和食物残渣。为帮助食客适应，2021年8月31日前不会采取纪律处分，只会劝导遵守规定。但从2021年9月1日起，对不听劝、不清理的人将执法。初犯者会收到书面警告。新加坡食品局也将与国家环境局合作，于今年第四季度逐步推行。环境局表示，这一举措在公共卫生危机背景下出台，是在多年广泛教育努力之后，旨在改变公共场所食客的行为与观念。

41.note: action will be taken — past participle after will be.

46.note: Agency will work with NEA — base verb, not works after will.

47.note: roll out the implementation — noun needed, not verb implement.

cloze: In his 1822 Master Town Plan, Sir Stamford Raffles allocated an area west of the Singapore River for a Chinese settlement. With numerous people arriving from China every day, he [Q51] to the conclusion that the Chinese would form the bulk of Singapore's population. At that point in [Q52], many Chinese were attracted to Singapore. They did not [Q53] spending long periods of time travelling all the way to Singapore in [Q54] of a better future which they could not have in China. Hence, Sir Stamford Raffles made the right judgement [Q55] by dedicating a special area to the Chinese.

Chinatown was eventually set up to meet the needs of the Chinese immigrants. In time to [Q56], many shops were set up to sell items that [Q57] to the taste of the Chinese. Business was brisk. As a [Q58], more and more shops were opened. At the same time, some thoughtful and kind businessmen decided to set up clan associations that would [Q59] care of the interest and well-being of the Chinese immigrants. [Q60] the immigrants felt lonely, they could always meet [Q61] with their friends at the clan association. As time went by, Chinatown became populated with immigrants from China.

Later, the original area [Q62] the Chinese communities settled down, was divided into zones for individuals [Q63] belonged to the same province and dialect group. The Cantonese occupied Temple Street. The Hokkiens were located [Q64] Telok Ayer Street and Hokkien Street, while the Teochews settled in South Canal Road. Chinatown is not only home to the Chinese, but also to several Indian and Malay traders. Thus, it is [Q65] surprise to see Indian temples and Muslim mosques in the area. Chinatown is certainly an interesting place to visit.
zh: 在1822年总镇计划中，莱佛士在新加坡河以西划出华人聚居区。随着每日大量华人抵达，他得出结论：华人将构成新加坡人口的主体。当时许多华人被新加坡吸引，他们不介意长途跋涉来这里寻找在中国无法拥有的更好未来。因此，莱佛士划出专门区域给华人是正确判断。
牛车水后来为满足华人移民需要而建立。久而久之，许多店铺出售符合华人口味的商品，生意兴旺。结果店铺越开越多。同时，一些善良商人设立会馆，照顾华人移民的利益与福祉。移民若感到孤独，总可以在会馆与朋友相聚。随着时间推移，牛车水住满来自中国各地的移民。
后来，华人社区最初定居的区域按省份与方言划分。广东人占据庙街，福建人位于直落亚逸街与福建街一带，潮州人住在南桥路。牛车水不仅是华人之家，也有印度和马来商贩，因此见到印度庙和清真寺并不奇怪。牛车水确是值得一游的地方。

51.concept: 一般过去时动词与习语搭配
51.note: 主语为单数代词 he（指代莱佛士），叙述 1822 年的历史，谓语动词采用一般过去时。与后面的介词短语 to the conclusion 完美组合，构成极高频常考的经典推理专属习语 came to the conclusion，意为“得出结论”。

52.concept: 历史时间特定习惯短语
52.note: 与其前置的介词短语 at that point in 完美结合。属于各类历史保育、建国发展史文章里高频考查的经典时间特定词组 at that point in time，意为“在那个历史时间节点/在那时”。

53.concept: 助动词后的动词原形与动名词搭配
53.note: 前面有否定助动词 did not，后面接动词原形，且后接动名词结构 spending。在早期移民远渡重洋的语境下，指他们完全“不介意（mind）”虚度大把时间在长途颠簸上，故填入动词原形（构成 did not mind doing 结构）。

54.concept: 经典复合介词短语搭配
54.note: 与其前置的介词 in 和后置的介词短语 of a better future 完美结合。构成全行业、各类移民史和迁徙文体中极其标志性的专属寻觅习语 in search of，意为背井离乡去“寻找”更美好的未来。

55.concept: 复合名词固定习惯搭配
55.note: 与前面的动词短语 made the right judgement 组合。在探讨重大历史决断的口语化及规范书面语境下，完美契合极高频专属搭配 made the right judgement call，意为莱佛士做出了一次极其高明的“断决/判定”。

56.concept: 经典时间推进习惯短语
56.note: 与其前置的时间短语 in time to 完美结合。属于英语中用于形容未来、久而久之时间演变的经典核心专属时间习语 in time to come，意为“在未来的日子里/久而久之”。

57.concept: 一般过去时动词与专属介词搭配
57.note: 由关系代词 that 引导的定语从句修饰复数先行词 items，且叙述历史背景，谓语动词用过去时。与后面的介词短语 to the taste 组合，构成极高频常考的经典商业供求短语 catered to，意为这些商铺旨在“迎合/满足”华人的口味（填入 suited 表达符合口味亦符合逻辑）。

58.concept: 篇章逻辑因果承接固定短语
58.note: 与其前置的介词短语 As a 完美结合，后面有逗号隔开。前文提到生意兴隆，此处引出水到渠成的结果：因此越来越多的店铺开张。完美契合标志性因果短语 As a result（结果/因此）。

59.concept: 情态动词后的短语动词原形搭配
59.note: 前面有情态助动词 would，后面必须接动词原形。与后面的介词短语 care of 完美组合，构成全行业最经典、最基础的核心专属短语动词 take care of，意为宗亲会成立的初衷是为了“照顾”华工的切身利益。

60.note: 引导时间/条件状语从句。用来连接前后两句，指代“当（When）”或者“每当（Whenever/If）”这些离乡背井的移民感到孤独无依时，他们总能去宗亲会倾诉，用作段落内的人情背景引入。位于句首需大写。

61.concept: 短语动词固定搭配形式
61.note: 与前面的动词原形 meet 极其后置的介词短语 with their friends 完美组合。构成社交会面、抱团取暖专属的高频特定短语 meet up with，表示和朋友们在此“碰头/聚会/抱团叙旧”。

62.concept: 关系副词引导定语从句
62.note: 引导限定性定语从句，修饰表示场所、居住区的先行词 the original area。华人群体在这些区域定居下来，在从句中充当特定的地点状语，故填入关系副词 where（或者介词短语 in which）。

63.concept: 定语从句关系代词形式
63.note: 引导限定性定语从句，修饰表示人类的复数先行词 individuals（个人/人们）。从句中缺少主语成分，且指代人，故固定填入关系代词 who 或者是 that。

64.concept: 地点街道专属介词搭配
64.note: 用来连接被动短语 were located 和后面的具体街道名称 Telok Ayer Street...。在新加坡规范英语和地理历史文体中，指代具体位于某某街、某某路这一确定空间，固定使用专属介词 at 或者是 along / on（此处 at 或者是 on 最符合官方阅卷标准）。

65.concept: 经典句型固定绝对否定搭配
65.note: 与其前置的系动词句型结构 it is 和后置的名词 surprise 完美结合。构成全行业说明文、游记文体中极高频出现的经典标志性断言句式 it is no surprise to see...，意为在这里看到印度庙和清真寺“一点也不令人感到奇怪（因为这里本就是多元文化交融之地）”。

66.concept: 句型转换 — With the early arrival（Noun phrase）
66.zh: 贵宾提早到达，主人一片慌乱。
66.note: 用 With the early + 名词（arrival）把两句合并为一句。
66.answer: With the early arrival of the guest of honour, the host was filled with panic.

67.concept: 间接引语 — exclaimed that（Reported speech）
67.zh: 黄先生兴奋地喊道，他迫不及待要在第二天去旅行。
67.note: 直接引语改间接引语：时态后移，tomorrow → the next day。
67.answer: In an excited voice, Mr Wong exclaimed that he could not wait to travel the next day.

68.concept: 被动语态 — was guided（Passive voice）
68.note: 主动改被动：The ship was guided … using searchlights。
68.answer: The ship was guided into the harbour using searchlights.

69.concept: 分词短语 — Separating … is（Participial subject）
69.zh: 隔开两间教室的是一道可移动隔断。
69.note: Separating … 作主语，谓语 is a movable partition。
69.answer: Separating the two classrooms is a movable partition.

70.concept: 倒装 — Had it not been for（Inverted conditional）
70.zh: 若不是服务太差，何女士本会买下那台微波炉。
70.note: Had it not been for + 名词：若非……就会（与事实相反）。
70.answer: Had it not been for the poor service, Mdm Ho would have bought the microwave.

lines.8: friends. Otherwise, he would be teased ceaselessly. It was all for fun and none of them

paragraphs.1: 2019年6月，一支少年足球队经历了一生难忘的冒险——一场他们永不会忘记的噩梦。训练结束后，男孩们与教练骑车进入林木茂密的山丘，目的地是男孩们常去的朗洞。
paragraphs.5: 快到洞口时，男孩们下车，把自行车留在废弃小屋旁。“走吧！”教练催促。男孩们兴奋地抢着第一个进洞；最后一个男孩拼命想追上并超过同伴，否则会被不停取笑。大家图个乐，从没人抱怨。而且第一个进洞的人还能从阿迪教练那里得到冰淇淋奖励。
paragraphs.11: 一进洞，男孩们像往常一样兴奋。他们拿着掉落的粗树枝和火把，小心走在狭窄蜿蜒的通道里。途中萨马德和约迪短暂停下，用口袋里的粉笔在洞壁上写下新队员的名字。他们越爬越深，兴高采烈地探索各个角落。他们不知道危险就在前方。
paragraphs.17: 正当他们准备返回洞口时，意想不到的事发生了。雷鸣般的轰响打破寂静，接着又一声再一声。胆小的约迪捂住耳朵，眼里涌泪。“呃……我想我们现在出不去了。”阿迪教练说。几乎立刻，水涌入洞中。约迪尖叫像婴儿一样哭。萨马德大笑。阿迪教练立刻狠狠瞪了他一眼。突发山洪使雨水灌满洞穴。
paragraphs.24: “快，我们必须往洞深处走！走路时紧紧牵住彼此的手。”阿迪教练说着，抓住约迪的手谨慎向前。全队迅速反应，他们蹚过及膝的水，越走越远以逃离洪水。过了一会儿，教练看见前方景象停住脚步。“看！我们安全了！”尽管疲惫不堪，大家仍坚持前进，很快停在小石台前。
paragraphs.31: 满怀希望，他们爬上石台躲避洪水。但快乐转瞬即逝——此刻水位开始上涨。“糟了！无路可逃！我们走到死胡同了！”萨马德喊道。约迪又哭起来。阿迪教练搂住他，大家只能挤在一起取暖。男孩们很害怕，但决心活下去，因为想再见到家人。
paragraphs.37: 注意到他们的焦虑，阿迪教练说：“你们必须保持冷静沉着，这样才能保存体力。”他们没有食物，但有稳定的水源——来自洞壁滴落的水珠。
paragraphs.41: 男孩们晚饭时还没回家，家人报警。警方与潜水员一起展开持续近一周的救援，他们并未放弃。幸运的是第六天，潜水员找到了要找的——手电光照亮令人震撼的一幕：男孩们从黑暗中走出来！失踪的男孩终于被找到了！

71.note:
1. 问进洞之前在做什么，看第2–3行。

  3. 证据：第2行 After their training session，第1行点明 junior football team。
  4. 答：他们刚结束足球训练。
answer: They were having their football training session.

  2. ① move deeper into the cave；② Hold each other's hands tightly。

76.note:

  2. (a) a nightmare（第2行）指这次被困洞中近一周的历险 → adventure of a lifetime … stuck in cave。
  3. (b) the unthinkable（第17行）指突发的 water gushing into the cave。
  4. (c) that（第28行）指教练看见的 small rocky ledge。

answer.76a: the adventure of a lifetime, when the boys and their coach was stuck in a cave for almost a week
answer.76b: the water gushing into the cave

77.note:
1. 范围：paragraph 4（约17–23行）与 paragraph 7（约37–40行），逐行判读。
  2. (a) False：约迪先哭是因害怕 rumbling sound（第18–19行），不单因教练说不能离开。
  3. (b) False：萨马德停笑因教练 deathly glare（第21–22行），文中未写内疚。
  4. (c) True：第39–40行有 steady supply of water from droplets — 不渴因有水源。
  5. 书写：每行先 T/F 再一句依据。

answer.77b: Jodi cried at first as he was afraid of the rumbling sound.
answer.77d: Samad stopped laughing at Jodi as coach Adi shot him a deathly glare.
answer.77f: They had a steady supply of water, which they got from the droplets of water dripping from the cave walls.

78.note:
1. 第24–30行教练表现：带领深走、牵手、发现石台、坚持前进。
  2. determined：疲惫仍 press on；responsible：抓住约迪、指挥全队。
  3. 勿选 fair/patient/proud/relaxed — 文中无充分证据。
  4. 勾选两项，拼写与 options 一致。

79.note:
1. 情况恶化 = 第33–40行：死胡同、约迪再哭、水位上升。
  2. 安抚① 第37–38行：要求 stay calm and composed 以保存体力。
  3. 安抚② 第34–35行：wrapped his arms around Jodi，huddle 取暖。
  4. 答出言语+行动两点更完整。
answer: He told the boys to stay calm and composed so that they would be able to conserve their energy. He also wrapped his arms around Jodi and huddled together with the boys to keep warm.

80.note:
1. 问男孩展现的一种价值观+文中证据。
  2. 第35–36行 determined to survive，想见家人 → Determination。
  3. 证据：近一周几乎无食物仍坚持（第42–43行 rescue 时间呼应）。
  4. 先写价值词，再引一句原文行为。
answer: Determination. They survived for almost a week without food. This proves that they had determination to survive as they wanted to see their family members again.
